uRos 2026 Tutorial - Paris" title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: images/title-fullpic-light.png data-background-size: cover data-background-position: center data-background-repeat: no-repeat format: revealjs: theme: - brand - custom.scss resources: - images/ revealjs-plugins: - tabset --- # Introduction {background-color='{{< brand color blue >}}' .bkg-buildings} ## About Us {.bkg-serpent} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width=33%} ![](images/StephanieZimmer_Headshot.jpeg){fig-align="center" width=200px}

::: :::: ::: {.notes} Each of us give a brief intro on our experience/background ::: ## Prerequisites {.bkg-left} **Tidyverse familiarity** ::: {.incremental} - Selecting a set of variables (`select(starts_with("TOT"))`) - Creating new variables with `mutate()` - Summarizing data with `summarize()` - Using `group_by()` with `summarize()` to create group summaries ::: ## Overview of tutorial {.bkg-trees} - At the end of this tutorial, you should be able to ::: {.incremental} - Specify a survey design in R to create a survey object - Calculate point estimates and their standard errors with survey data - Create tables and graphs incorporating survey data and standard errors ::: ## Logistics {.bkg-right} - We will be using Posit Cloud for exercises - All materials are found at: - (Site) - (Source) ## Libraries Needed for Today {.bkg-ship} _Note: These are already installed in Posit Cloud_ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(survey) library(srvyr) library(gt) library(sf) library(rnaturalearth) library(leaflet) ``` ::: ## R Packages for Survey Analysis {.bkg-ship} ::::: {.columns} :::: {.column width=49%} ::: {.fragment} - {survey} package first on CRAN in 2003 - descriptive analysis - statistical testing - modeling - weighting ::: :::: ::: {.column width=2%} ::: ::: {.column width=49%} ::: {.fragment} - {srvyr} package first on CRAN in 2016 - “wrapper” for {survey} with {tidyverse}-style syntax - only descriptive analysis ::: :::: ::::: ## Why use {srvyr} over {survey}? ::: {.incremental} - Use the pipe function `%>%` or `|>` - Ability to use tidy selection - Functions follow `snake_case` convention ::: # Comparison of {dplyr} and {srvyr} Functions {background-color='{{< brand color blue >}}' .bkg-buildings} ## Apply {dplyr} functions to survey objects - A few functions in {srvyr} have counterparts in {dplyr} - `dplyr::summarize()` and `srvyr::summarize()` - `dplyr::group_by()` and `srvyr::group_by()` - Based on the object class, R will recognize which package to use ## Using `summarize()` to calculate mean and median ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Tibble: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|1|2,4|3|"} towny %>% summarize( area_mean = mean(land_area_km2, na.rm=TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 1 area_mean 1 373. ``` ::: ::: ### Survey object: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} anes_des %>% summarize( age_mean = survey_mean(Age, na.rm=TRUE), ) ``` ::: ::: ## Filtering and Selecting ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Tibble: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} towny %>% filter(csd_type == "township") %>% select(csd_type, name) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 195 × 2 csd_type name 1 township Addington Highlands 2 township Adelaide Metcalfe 3 township Adjala-Tosorontio 4 township Admaston/Bromley 5 township Alberton 6 township Alfred and Plantagenet 7 township Algonquin Highlands 8 township Alnwick/Haldimand 9 township Amaranth 10 township The Archipelago # ℹ 185 more rows ``` ::: ::: ### Survey object: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} anes_des %>% filter(EducationGroup == "Graduate") %>% select(Sex) ``` ::: ::: ## Grouping ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Tibble: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} towny %>% group_by(csd_type) %>% summarize(area_mean = mean(land_area_km2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 5 × 2 csd_type area_mean 1 city 498. 2 municipality 607. 3 town 183. 4 township 363. 5 village 23.0 ``` ::: ::: ### Survey object: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} anes_des %>% group_by(EducationGroup) %>% summarize(age_mean = survey_mean(Age, na.rm=TRUE)) ``` ::: ::: ## Using {srvyr} functions on non-survey objects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} towny %>% summarize(area_mean = survey_mean(land_area_km2)) ``` ::: . . . ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `summarize()`: ℹ In argument: `area_mean = survey_mean(land_area_km2)`. Caused by error in `cur_svy()`: ! Survey context not set ``` ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
